title:
FRACTIONS, DECIMALS AND PERCENTAGES
(CONVERTING BETWEEN FDP)
objective: LO: I can convert fluently between fractions, decimals and percentages.

content.text: Converting means writing a number in a DIFFERENT form without changing its value. Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways to write the same amount.
Key fact: To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. To convert a decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100.

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Fraction → Decimal: divide top by bottom. Decimal → Percentage: × 100. Percentage → Fraction: write over 100 and simplify.
key_idea.caption: Divide, then multiply by 100

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – decimal to percentage
modelled_examples.question: Convert 0.35 to a percentage
modelled_examples.explanation: Multiply the decimal by 100 and add the % symbol.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – percentage to fraction
modelled_examples.question: Convert 45% to a fraction in simplest form
modelled_examples.explanation: Write over 100, then simplify by dividing both by the HCF (5).

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – fraction to percentage
modelled_examples.question: Convert &frac{7}{20} to a percentage
modelled_examples.explanation: Convert to decimal first (divide), then multiply by 100.

practice.heading: Fraction to decimal
practice.instruction: Convert each fraction to a decimal by dividing the numerator by the denominator.

practice.heading: Decimal to percentage
practice.instruction: Convert each decimal to a percentage by multiplying by 100.

practice.heading: Percentage to fraction
practice.instruction: Convert each percentage to a fraction in its simplest form. Write over 100 then simplify.

practice.heading: Fraction to percentage
practice.instruction: Convert each fraction to a percentage. Divide first, then multiply by 100.

practice.heading: Mixed conversions
practice.instruction: Convert each value to the other two forms (fraction, decimal, percentage).

problems.text:
A shop offers a ¼ off sale. The sale sign says “20% off everything!”
Is the sale sign correct? Show your working to explain why or why not.

Three students scored the following on different tests:
Amy: 17 out of 20    Ben: 0.82    Clara: 78%
Who got the highest score? Convert all to the same form to compare.
